o: The compiler checks generic types and removes them, so they are absent at run time
The JVM deletes unused generic classes from memory when needed
Generic types are replaced by arrays after class loading
A runtime check that rejects objects of the wrong generic type
questions.w: At run time `List<String>` and `List<Integer>` are both `List`. Casts are inserted by the compiler where needed.

questions.q: Why does `List<Number> nums = new ArrayList<Integer>();` not compile?
o: Generics are invariant: `List<Integer>` is not a `List<Number>`
`Integer` is not a subclass of `Number` in Java
`ArrayList` cannot hold boxed numbers at all
The diamond operator is missing from the right side
questions.w: Otherwise you could add a `Double` through the `List<Number>` view and corrupt the list of Integers.

questions.q: A method only reads numbers from a collection. Which parameter type is the most flexible?
o: `Collection<? extends Number>`
`Collection<Number>`
`Collection<? super Number>`
`Collection<Object>`
questions.w: PECS: Producer Extends. The collection produces values, so `extends` accepts `List<Integer>`, `List<Double>` and more.

questions.q: A method only adds `Integer` values into a collection passed by the caller. Which parameter type fits?
o: `Collection<? super Integer>`
`Collection<? extends Integer>`
`Collection<?>`
`Collection<int>`
questions.w: Consumer Super. A `List<Number>` or `List<Object>` can safely accept Integers, and primitives cannot be type arguments.

questions.q: Which statement does NOT compile because of erasure?
o: `T item = new T();`
`List<String> names = new ArrayList<>();`
`T item = clazz.cast(obj);`
`static <T> T first(List<T> xs)`
questions.w: `T` is unknown at run time. Pass a `Class<T>` or a `Supplier<T>` instead.

questions.q: What happens with `Object[] a = new String[1]; a[0] = 42;`?
o: It compiles and throws `ArrayStoreException` at run time
It fails to compile because of a type mismatch
It compiles and silently stores the number
It compiles and converts 42 to the string "42"
questions.w: Arrays are covariant and reified. Generic collections are invariant and checked at compile time instead.

questions.q: Why is `<T extends Comparable<T>> T max(T a, T b)` needed instead of `<T> T max(T a, T b)`?
o: The bound lets the method call `compareTo` on `T`
Unbounded type parameters cannot be used in methods
The bound makes the method faster at run time
Without the bound the method would not be generic
questions.w: An unbounded `T` is only known to be an `Object`. A bound tells the compiler which methods are available.

o: Arrays need run-time element types, which erasure removes for `List<String>`
Arrays of lists are forbidden in all Java versions
`List` is an interface and interfaces cannot be array elements
The array size must be a constant known at compile time
questions.w: Allowing it would let a `List<Integer>` into the array unchecked. Use `List<List<String>>` instead.
